title: Reconcile burst-quota snapshots after service-account rotation causing billing drift
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported incorrect remaining burst quota and unexpected billing spikes after rotating service-account keys for delegated subaccounts. Investigation shows a race between the key-rotation propagation job and the billing aggregation snapshotter resulting in double-counted delta snapshots and transient attribution to the old tenant id.

Root cause hypothesis: During rotation we emit a key-swap event that updates the tenant->service-account mapping in the auth metadata store. The billing snapshotter consumes usage events from kafka and attaches attribution by querying the auth cache. If the snapshotter processes events for the same time window before the mapping update has fully propagated to all cache nodes, it will produce a delta snapshot that attributes usage to both the old and new tenant keys (duplicate deltas). Additionally, the rate-limiter's tenant counters are occasionally reconstructed from these inconsistent snapshots, causing temporary quota bleed and doubled billing for a short window.

Why this matters: Affected customers experienced incorrect quota enforcement and overbilling for the rotation window. This breaks our billing guarantees and could trigger escalations for enterprise customers on Dedicated/Private deployments where rotations are managed by customer automation.

Scope: Initial sampling shows 8 customers in the past 30 days (mix of hosted and dedicated) had non-zero duplicate delta snapshots; estimated revenue impact small but customer trust risk high.

Work planned: 1) Patch the snapshotter to read attribution ids from the kafka event envelope (which is immutable) rather than the cache for the same timestamp window when available, falling back to cache only for late-arriving events. 2) Add an idempotency layer: de-duplicate delta snapshots by (tenant_id, window_start, source_offset). 3) Harden key-rotation propagation: publish a rotation-complete marker that snapshotter can check for active windows. 4) Backfill reconciliation job to scan last 72 hours for duplicate deltas and emit compensating corrections for billing and rate-limiter counters.

Notes on trade-offs: Reading attribution from immutable event envelopes increases coupling to the event schema but avoids cache staleness. The idempotency table adds storage and write/read overhead but is limited by retention of windowed snapshots. Backfill will need careful throttling to avoid load spikes on aggregation and billing services.

Contact points: Eng (metering infra) + billing ops + customer success for affected customers.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a service-account bound to a subaccount and generate API key A.
2) Issue steady burst traffic (simulate repeated small requests to exhaust burst quota) for 10 minutes under key A.
3) Trigger service-account rotation to replace key A with key B via the rotation endpoint.
4) Immediately after rotation, continue traffic under key B for the same tenant for the next 10 minutes.
5) Observe billing snapshots and rate-limiter tenant counters for overlapping windows via the billing-dashboard (grafana link) and aggregation logs.

Expected: continuous attribution to the single tenant with no duplicated delta snapshots.
    Observed: overlapping window produced two deltas attributing to both old and new key mapping, leading to doubled quota decrement in some rate-limiter replicas.

timeline_updates: 2025-02-15: Ticket created after on-call escalations from billing-ops. Initial triage indicates cache propagation window as likely cause.
2025-02-17: Reproduced locally with rotation harness. Confirmed duplicate delta snapshots when rotation occurs mid-window.
2025-02-19: Design review with metering and auth teams. Agreed patch approach: use immutable event envelope for attribution, plus idempotency table.
2025-02-22: Hotfix deployed to snapshotter in staging to prefer event-envelope attribution. End-to-end tests added for rotation edge cases.
2025-02-26: Begin running backfill reconciliation in low-traffic window for last 72 hours on canary cluster; monitoring CPU/spike metrics closely.
acceptance_criteria: Patch merged and deployed to production snapshotter that prevents duplicate delta creation for rotation windows.
Idempotency de-dup table in place and validated with synthetic replays without false positives.
Backfill job completed for affected 72-hour window with corrections applied and billing ops sign-off obtained.
No customers show duplicate delta spikes for two weeks after deployment; monitoring alerts cleared.
Notes and runbook updated: rotation checklist includes publishing rotation-complete marker and snapshotter fallback behavior.
